dish.title: Thai Moo Ping: Grilled Pork Skewers with Sticky Rice and Jaew Dipping Sauce

recipe_version.title: Thai Moo Ping: Grilled Pork Skewers with Sticky Rice and Jaew Dipping Sauce
recipe_version.description: Bangkok street-style pork skewers: thin slices of pork shoulder marinated in garlic, cilantro stems, white pepper, palm sugar, soy sauce, fish sauce, and coconut milk, grilled and basted until caramelized. Served with steamed sticky rice, cucumber, and a tangy chile-lime jaew sauce with toasted rice powder.

ingredients.name: cilantro
ingredients.note: stems for the marinade, leaves for the jaew and garnish

ingredients.name: palm sugar or light brown sugar
ingredients.display_name: palm sugar or light brown sugar

ingredients.name: fish sauce
ingredients.display_name: fish sauce whose label lists anchovy, salt, and sugar only

ingredients.name: canned coconut milk
ingredients.note: 1/3 cup marinade, the rest for basting

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: hot from the tap, for soaking the rice

steps.title: Prep the marinade
steps.body: Pound or finely mince the garlic and the cilantro stems with the white pepper to a coarse paste. Stir in the palm sugar, soy sauce, 2 tbsp fish sauce, 1/3 cup coconut milk, and the oil. Slice the very cold pork thin, 1/8 inch thick, and toss it in the marinade. Rinse the sticky rice until the rinse runs clear and cover it with 6 cups hot tap water.

steps.title: Marinate and soak
steps.body: Refrigerate the pork and leave the rice to soak for 1 hour. Soak 12 bamboo skewers in a tray at the same time.

steps.title: Steam the sticky rice
steps.body: Bring 8 cups water to a boil in a 5-quart pot. Drain the rice, spread it in a cheesecloth-lined steamer basket, set it over the pot, cover, and steam 25 minutes, flipping the mass of rice halfway, until translucent and chewy. This runs inside steps 4 to 6 (overlap stated).

steps.title: Make the jaew and thread the skewers
steps.body: Toast 1 tbsp uncooked rice in a dry 8-inch skillet over medium, shaking, until deep golden, about 5 minutes; grind to a coarse powder. Stir 1 tbsp fish sauce, the lime juice, chile flakes, shallot, toasted rice powder, and chopped cilantro leaves together. Thread the pork onto the skewers, bunching it slightly. Discard the marinade.

steps.title: Preheat the grill
steps.body: Preheat the grill on medium-high, lid closed, for 10 minutes, then clean and oil the grate. Slice the cucumber meanwhile.

steps.title: Grill
steps.body: Grill the skewers, turning every 2 minutes and basting with the remaining coconut milk, until caramelized, charred at the edges, and 145 F, about 10 minutes.

steps.title: Serve
steps.body: Pack the sticky rice into small baskets or bowls and serve with the skewers, cucumber, and jaew for dipping.

equipment: steamer basket or bamboo steamer with a lid set over a 5-quart pot
cheesecloth or a clean thin towel
mortar and pestle or spice grinder

recipe_version.dietary_label_note: Unconditional dairy_free: the creaminess in the marinade is coconut milk. Fish sauce is a seasoning, so the fish label is not used.
allergen_notes: Soy and wheat from the soy sauce.
The fish sauce label lists anchovy, salt, and sugar, with no shrimp or shellfish.
Coconut (coconut milk) is not a FlavorWeave allergen token; diners avoiding coconut should skip this dish.
No egg, milk, sesame, shellfish, or nuts.

near_duplicate_review: Compared with nigerian-beef-suya-skewers: pork with a sweet coconut-soy marinade and sticky rice, not beef with peanut spice. Compared with vietnamese-bun-cha: skewered grilled pork with sticky rice and jaew, not patties in a dipping broth with noodles. Compared with hawaiian-huli-huli-chicken in this wave: pork skewers with sticky rice and a chile-lime sauce, not glazed chicken thighs with pineapple.
